label: text
text: A twenty-five ft. frontage in Sydney was sold at auction for $55,600.

label: text
text: During the absence of Mr. H. Holyout, Mr. F. L. Lewis will be in charge of the Hongkong Office of Messrs. Holyout and Assey.

label: text
text: The Eastern Extinction: Aus-fialastic and China Telegraph Co., Ltd., notify that normal working with Shanghai and beyond has been re-established.

label: text
text: Tuesday's return of notifiable diseases in the Colony comprised only one case of smallpox. The patient, a "Chinese," is an arrival in Hongkong and not a resident.

label: text
text: People afflicted with Asthma should “hum” through their noses. It would help them overcome its and eventually will-cure the disease entirely, according to Professor Horbuser, well known Vienna Laryngologist.

label: text
text: "Vienna coffee houses are in danger of becoming Americanized!" is the cry in the famous old capital of the Hapsburgs, whose coffee houses are tradition the world over. The issue at stake is whether waiters shall discard their dress suits and tuxedos for short white coats.

text: One of several pigs which naided the garden of Mujajor George-Hutchinson at Camelford Cornwall.

text:
A Blackburn grocer, summoned for selling goods on early closing day, said: "I have committed an offence in the eyes of man, but not in the eyes of my Heavenly Father, who said: 'Six days shall thou beeng and do all thy work, but rest on the seventh day.' I try to do that." He was fined five shillings.
"No no Nanette" has been running in London for a year.

label: text
text: "She called me a teetotaller, and I look upon that as an insult."—Man at Tottenham Police Court.

label: text
text: No youths at Meashum, Leicestershire, are applying for apprenticeships to tradesmen, although they may under a charity to this village.

label: text
text: Building trade rates to apply to the erection of all houses was the gist of a resolution passed by a Scottish Labour conference at Glasgow.

label: text
text: Post Office savings deposits on December 31, were £285,400,-000, Government stock sold £314,-918,471, and holders' credit £188,775,460.

label: text
text: In an attempt to lift South Wales from "iniquity," magistrates who consider ordinary dancing as "dangerous" excitement," barbaric" and "sensuous," have forbidden this. "indiscreet" pastime late at night.

label: text
text: It is reported from Mysore that at a village, a few miles from that city, some unknown person has poisoned 25 wild monkeys. Orthodox Hindus who venerate the monkey, dressed the bodies in funeral garments and took them in religious procession through the streets of the city to the denomination ground and disposed of them with Shastrie ceremonially. The outraged Hinds are looking for the poisoner.

label: text
text: "Let who will make the laws of a country, if I may control the cinemas." Mr. Snowden, ex-Chancellor of the Exchequer, thus modernised the old adage at the annual dinner of the Citizen-tograph Exhibitors Association at the Hotel Victoria. Tax oil entertainments was bad, anid violated all sound financial policy, he said. It discouraged a legitimate and very useful form of enjoyment. Thirty million people went to the cinema, and he believed that it did more than any other agency to promote temperance and sobriety.

label: text
text: There is to be another attempt to show that Shakespeare derived from factors other than rustic and common. The Cambridge University Press will publish "A Chapter in the Early Life of Shakespeare," by Arthur Gray, in which the author will endavour to show that Shakespeare did not spend all his youth at Stratford, but passed part of it at Polesworth, Warwickshire, a literary resort of the period.

label: doc_title
text: SOCIAL AND PERSONAL.

label: text
text: The average salary of maddservants in Tokyo is ¥1.5 a month with board and sleeping accommodation charged to the employer, according to statistics. The demand is exceeding the supply, it is announced.

label: text
text: Dr. C. N. Abraham, second son of the late Rev. S. Abraham, has been appointed Assistant Health Officer for Kinta.

label: text
text: A proposal that all cats should be registered by the police, for a shilling fee, and weare an identity disc, was rejected by a Glasgow Corporation committee. The project was put forward by the local branch of the Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals. The medical officer reported that the spread of disease had not been traced to cats to any serious extent, and that compulsory registration might lead to increasing rats and mice.

label: text
text: A Berlin cable to "The Daily Chronicle" says the Soviets have decided to permit women to be officers on ships of their "mercantile marine." One woman is to be a naval architect in State shipbuilding yards; another is appointed to be captain of a steamer. She will be the first woman to command a ship of the Black Sea fleet.

label: text
text: The £20,000 worth of American railway bonds found by a girl's cinema attendant in a Cheltenham picture house have been claimed. A clerk in a local business house visited Cheltenham Police Station and said, although he was not the actual owner, he had them in his possession and dropped them while visiting the pictures.

label: text
text: Nearly half the prisons in the country have been closed down in the last 12 years in consequence of the enormous decrease in the prison population.

label: text
text: Me. G. J. Dickson has been appointed hon. secretary of the Malacca Branch of the Malayan Agri-Horticultural Association.

label: text
text: Mr. Charles Christian Heidsieck, of the well-known firm of Charles Heidsieck, Rheims, champagne growers is at present in Penang on a short visit.

label: text
text: Will the provisional title "Queen Mary as Working Woman," a remarkable and unconventional book by a new authoress will be published this spring.

label: text
text: Seventy thousand children were entertained by the Salvation Army at banquets in various parts of the country in celebration of General Booth's seventieth birthday.

label: text
text: At Belmont Parish, Church, Glasgow, on the 4th instant, the marriage took place of Mr. James Whyte, of Singapore, eldest son of Mr. and Mrs. Whyte, Friarscroft, Renfrew, to Miss Mona Hardie Macnie, M.B., Ch. B., only daughter of the Rev. R. L. Macnie and Mrs. Macnie, Loth. Sutherland.

label: text
text: Doubleday, Page & Company, are strongly opposed to Mrs. Conrad's book about her distinguished husband, which is regarded as too intimate and too trivial and not calculated to do Mr. Conrad's reputation any good. Among other things, Mrs. Conrad told how her husband would monopolise the bathroom, splashing in the tub, to the exclusion of their guests.

label: text
text: H.S.H. Princess Phorn, a daughter of H.R.H. Prince Damrong, who has received a Siamese Red Cross scholarship, left for Manila on the 5th instant with Dr. and Mrs. Lowell to take up a course of medical studies. This will be the first occasion on which a princess has left Siam to prosecute her studies.

label: text
text: The "Comptesse de Flandres" steamer, which went ashore near Beachy, Head on December 30, has been refloated and safely berthed.

label: text
text: The University College Charity "Rag" at Nottingham realised £1,400—a record.

label: text
text: The Earl of Craven, for whom a deportation warrant was issued in Washington, in connection with the immigration trouble.

label: text
text: Dr. S. W. Eveson is appointed to officute as "Health Officer, Malacca, with effect from March 25.

label: text
text: Colonel Russell Brown leaves the Colony to-morrow for Peking. This will mean his withdrawal from the tennis tournament.

label: text
text: Lady Gregory, who was one of the founders of the Abbey Theatre, is writing her reminiscences. Two new plays by her are to be published shortly. Lady Gregory's "Hyacinth Hvaley" was one of the plays performed at the recent celebration of the coming of age of the Abbey Theatre.

label: text
text: Baroness Clifton is not the only society girl "to take up the law, The Hon. Sylvia Moulton, the 23-years-old daughter of the late Lord Moulton, the famous judge, has taken her law degree at Cambridge, and has even eaten her dinners at the Temple, though few of her associates, reallsed who she was.

label: text
text: Still another Hamlet, this time an Italian version of the great English classic, will be seen this season in London where John Barrymore's interpretation and the plus four rendition already have been applauded. Ruggero Ruggeri, one of the best actors in Italy, will give "Amloto" at the St. James Theatre and later at Oxford, Cambridge, Edinburgh and Glass.

label: text
text: Claiming to be the tallest people in England, Mr. and Mrs. L. G. Murray are starting from Plymouth on two years' cycling tour of the world.

label: text
text: Mrs. Henry Allhusen is the donor of £4,000 for a National Home of Health as headquarters of the New Health Society, as a memorial to her husband and children.

label: text
text: Sight has been given to three sisters and their brother, all born blind and all grown up, by Dr. C. M. Hawes, of the Hawes-Marple Hospital at Huntington, West Virginia.

label: text
text: Students of the Labour College protest against the project to convert Easton Lodge, the gift of the Countess of Warwick, into a Labour University, and suggest a convalescent home.

label: text
text: Tolstoy's centenary falls in 1928 and the Bolshevik authorities in Moscow are preparing a complete and uncensored edition of his works in twenty volumes. A million copies will be printed.

label: text
text: The Beverly Hills estate of Douglas Fairbanks and Mary Pickford is to be sold. They plan to build a Spanish hacienda farther back in the hills. The couple will leave soon on a tour of Europe.

label: text
text: Ewell (Surrey) Congregational Church, which has celebrated its diamond jubilee, was originally started in 1825 by an Ewell servant girl, Mary Wallis, who built a small chapel out of her savings.

label: text
text: Mr. Francis Eden Lacey, who has been secretary of the M.C.C. since 1898, tendered his resignation to the committee some time ago, but at their request he is "carrying on" until the end of the season.

label: text
text:
Modern fashions were roundly condemned by Mr. William Haworth in his presidential address to the Bolton Master Cotton Spinners' Association. It used to be said, he observed, that the adding of two inches to a China-man's shirt would do a great deal of good to the Lancashire cotton trude. So extreme had fashion become in this country that sometimes the women folk almost resembled Eye. As time went on they would probably get back to a saner style of dress, which would be more advantageous to Lancashire.
